# Apple Cider Vinegar

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="apple-cider-vinegar-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="apple-cider-vinegar-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="apple-cider-vinegar-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Apple Cider Vinegar in the HMI library has 23 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and nickel from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ndung&#39;u K, Hibdon S, Flegal AR · 2004</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Determination of lead in vinegar by ICP-MS and GFAAS: evaluation of different sample preparation procedures</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Talanta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury and nickel, in 23 results from 3 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ndung&#39;u K, Hibdon S, Flegal AR · 2004</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Determination of lead in vinegar by ICP-MS and GFAAS: evaluation of different sample preparation procedures</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Talanta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the apple Cider Vinegar was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ndung&#39;u K, Hibdon S, Flegal AR · 2004</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Determination of lead in vinegar by ICP-MS and GFAAS: evaluation of different sample preparation procedures</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Talanta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ndung&#39;u K, Hibdon S, Flegal AR · 2004</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Determination of lead in vinegar by ICP-MS and GFAAS: evaluation of different sample preparation procedures</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Talanta</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ndungu2004-lead-vinegar-icpms-gfaas">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Acosta et al. 1993 reported lead at 440 µg/kg (mean ± 80 SD) and cadmium at 22 µg/kg (mean ± 8 SD) in apple Cider Vinegar, as sold from apple vinegar.<sup class="cite">[[sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Acosta A, Diaz C, Hardisson A, Gonzalez D · 1993</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Levels of Cd, Pb, and Ni in Different Types of Vinegars</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/acosta1993-cd-pb-ni-vinegar-types">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the apple Cider Vinegar came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

Results stay on the basis each source reports: as sold or fresh weight, dry weight, or unstated. Dry-weight, as-sold and unstated results are never pooled, and no moisture conversion is applied.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-apple-cider-vinegar" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-apple-cider-vinegar-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of apple cider vinegar, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>
